required_behavior: Introduce one small raw-record collector in the allowed file. Open records in binary unbuffered mode, request at most RECORD_LIMIT+1 (16385) bytes total per collection, close on every path, and reject len(raw)>RECORD_LIMIT with a specific record-overflow failure before decoding, splitlines, JSON parsing or routing checks. Count every raw byte, including newlines. Do not read to EOF, iterate lines, retry beyond the cap, or rely on stat-size checks.

Replace both current records.read_bytes() sites with this collector. Split/parse only returned in-bound bytes; remove the misleading sum-of-line-lengths size test. Retain existing record counts/content checks. Every newly added record read must also use the collector; centralization makes every read path auditable.

Add only closed --scenario values records-exact-limit and records-one-over. Each uses existing fixtures, actual adapter, native sandbox and shared bounded_run for one normal success invocation; verify unchanged output/status and cleanup first. Bound-read the produced record file, then append only enough newline bytes to reach 16384 or 16385 respectively. Reject unexpected initial size; never truncate records or accept user-selected sizes/content. Exercise the same raw collector again on the resulting file.

For these controls only, persist a small record-bound.json beneath validated output on success/failure: scenario, observed byte count from the actual capped read, limit, bounds outcome, protocol_evaluated=false, original failure and existing invocation lifecycle state. Capture overflow observation before raising; never infer it from the scenario. Exact-limit returns zero only for bounds acceptance at 16384; one-over returns nonzero with record-overflow at 16385. Padding is boundary-test data: do not parse it or require it to satisfy record count/routing rules. This receipt is not result.json or routing acceptance.
